game_start.text: Hi. I'm INTI, the voice of the base. On Mars you walk a little lighter.
You can move now. If you want a hint, press Tab.
This is your base. I watch the oxygen, energy, and radiation shielding.

first_outside.text: You left the base area. Outside, the suit uses oxygen faster.
Outside, the ground is Mars. It is very cold, and the habitat is the covered place.
The base is behind you. You can go on or turn back. The water on Mars is frozen.

oxygen_low.text: Oxygen dropped under a quarter. Outside, the suit uses it faster.
There is little air left in the reserve. Every minute away from the base matters more.
Watch the cyan bar. If it hits zero, the mission stops and asks for a rescue.

energy_low.text: Energy is low. The panels charge the battery when the sun reaches them.
The battery is low. Dust on the panels makes them charge less.
The yellow bar is weak. At night, each module that is on uses some of that energy.

food_low.text: There is little food left. The greenhouse can add some if it has energy.
The green bar is low. At dinner, a bigger meal fills more and costs more.
Food is tight. A harvest moves that bar.

new_day.text: Day {day} is starting. On Mars the day lasts a little longer than on Earth.
Good morning. The three bars are still up there: oxygen, energy, and shielding.
Another day at the base. Last night is written in the journal.

before_decision.text: There is a decision. I tell you the cost; the choice is yours.
Read the options calmly. Each one moves the bars a little.
There is not just one answer. Think about what the base needs most today.

event_dust_storm.text: Dust arrived. It sticks to the panels and takes away their power.
The sky filled with dust. While it lasts, the panels see less sun.
The dust can last more than a day. In that time the panels make less.

event_solar_storm.text: There is a solar storm. The habitat covers you better than the suit alone.
The Sun sent out a burst. Inside the habitat there is more protection.
This storm does not look like rain. The shelter is the habitat.

event_earth_message.text: A message arrived from Earth. The signal takes time: it is not instant.
They are writing from home. The message traveled for several minutes to get here.
There is news from Earth. The antenna is for answering. Without it, you can leave the reply written down.

event_panel_fail.text: A panel is not turning well. If it stays like that, it will make less power for a couple of days.
A panel has a fault. Going out to look at it uses oxygen. Leaving it keeps it weak.
The panel needs attention. One path uses air; the other leaves less energy.

event_harvest.text: There are plants ready in the greenhouse.
Time to look at the harvest. Cutting today gives food now. Letting it grow changes tomorrow's.
The greenhouse potatoes follow a real idea: soil like Mars soil, with compost.

event_meteorite.text: A little rock from the sky hit a module. It is not huge.
A small meteor touched the base. Repairing uses supplies. Isolating the module leaves it still.
You can patch the hit, or isolate the module. Each path changes the base in a different way.

rescue.text: A resource hit zero. We stop and ask for a rescue. You are safe.
A bar emptied. Help is coming. What matters is that you are all right.
We started the rescue protocol. The mission stops and you are safe.

mission_complete.text: You reached the end of the days. The mission is over.
You finished the mission. In the summary you will see your decisions.
The mission days are over. Now you can see how it went.

hints.text: Oxygen is under 25. Outside it drops faster. The habitat looks after it better.
Energy is under 25. If dust is on the panels, they charge less.
Food is under 25. The greenhouse and the night meal move that bar.
There is dust in the air. The panels make less power while the dust covers them.
There is a solar storm. The habitat protects you more than being outside.
You are outside the base area. The suit uses oxygen faster here.
You can walk, look at a module with E, and sleep in the bed to end the Day. Tab asks for a hint.

thin_air.text: The air on Mars is very thin and has almost no oxygen. That is why we live in a habitat and go out in a suit.

sol_length.text: A day on Mars lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes, a little longer than on Earth. Here we call it a Day.

gravity.text: Mars gravity is lower than Earth's: you would weigh less than half. Walking feels different.

dust_power.text: Mars dust sticks to the solar panels and takes away their power. Sometimes the wind cleans them a little.
dust_power.credit: NASA (missions with panels, such as InSight)

water_ice.text: Mars has water ice, mostly at the poles and under the ground in other places. It is not a river: it is frozen.

comms_delay.text: A message between Mars and Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes one way, depending on how far apart they are that day. It is not instant.

cold.text: Mars is usually very cold, often below minus 60 degrees. The habitat covers us from that and from the wind.

plants.text: On Earth, scientists have already grown plants in soil like Mars soil, with compost. In the game, the greenhouse potato follows that idea.
